title: feat(sandboxes): run every timeout in 10-minute steps
author: voodoohop

gist.summary: Sandbox timeouts now use 10-minute leases: timeouts of 10 minutes or less are paid up front, while longer timeouts keep the sandbox until its requested end, whether that is an hour or a month. Previously, timeouts within E2B's 24-hour run were paid up front and only longer runs were kept in hourly steps. Gen's renewal cron runs every 5 minutes instead of 10 and renews whenever doing so adds time. The dashboard replaces its 24-hour explanation with the timeout end and hourly Pollen cost, shows each template's hourly price, and reads per-vCPU and per-GB prices from `/pricing`. Running “Until I stop it” sandboxes gain “Set time limit,” which sets a timeout from now through `/timeout` and can shorten the keep. Sandbox list responses and `GET /sandboxes/:id` now use `endAt` for the requested timeout end rather than the paid-ahead lease end; `keptUntil` and `/pricing`'s `maxRunSeconds` are removed. Polli drops its 24-hour cutoff and reads that same `endAt`; the sandbox docs are updated. Kept sandboxes have at most 10 minutes paid ahead: if two cron ticks are missed, an auto-pausing sandbox can pause until the next tick resumes it. The docs specify `lifecycle: { onTimeout: "pause" }` for E2B SDK users.
